value.zh: 下邳獻王晃字子明，魏封武始亭侯，拜黃門侍郎，改封西安男，出為東莞太守。
value.en: Sima Huang, styled Ziming, began as Wushi ting marquis, yellow-gate gentleman, Xi'an baron, then Dongguan governor.
value.literal: Prince Xian of Xiapi Huang courtesy Ziming was enfeoffed Marquis of Wushi precinct in Wei, appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, changed to Baron of Xi'an, and went out as governor of Dongguan.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封下邳王，邑五千一百七十六戶，泰始二年就國。
value.en: Sima Yan invested him at Xiapi with 5,176 households in 266.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiapi with five thousand one hundred seventy-six households and proceeded to his state in Taishi year two.

value.zh: 太原烈王瓌，字子泉，魏長樂亭侯，改封貴壽鄉侯。
value.en: Sima Gui, styled Ziquan, held Changle ting then Guishou township under Wei.
value.literal: Prince Lie of Taiyuan Gui courtesy Ziquan was Marquis of Changle precinct in Wei and changed to Marquis of Guishou village.

value.zh: 曆振威將軍，秘書監，封固始子。
value.en: He rose through display-might general and palace librarian to Gushi viscount.
value.literal: He successively held General Who Displays Might, Palace Library Supervisor, and was enfeoffed Viscount of Gushi.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封太原王，邑五千四百九十六戶，泰始二年就國。
value.en: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he enfeoffed him as Prince of Taiyuan with 5,496 households; in Taishi year two, he went to his state.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he enfeoffed him as Prince of Taiyuan with 5,496 households; in Taishi year two, he went to his state.

value.zh: 四年入朝，賜袞冕之服，遷東中郎將。
value.en: Year four brought court robes and eastern gentleman-general rank.
value.literal: In the fourth year he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state; he was promoted General of the Eastern Gentlemen.

value.zh: 十年薨，詔曰：「瑰乃心忠篤，智器雅亮。
value.en: In the tenth year he died; an edict said, 'Gui's heart was loyal and earnest; intellect and capacity were elegant and bright.
value.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict said, 'Gui's heart was loyal and earnest; intellect and capacity were elegant and bright.

value.zh: 歷位文武，有幹事之績。
value.en: He successively held civil and military posts and had achievements in handling affairs.
value.literal: He successively held civil and military posts and had achievements in handling affairs.

value.zh: 出臨封土，夷夏懷附，鎮守許都，思謀可紀。
value.en: Going out he faced his enfeoffment lands and barbarians and Chinese cherished allegiance; guarding Xu capital his designs merit record.
value.literal: Going out he faced his enfeoffment lands and barbarians and Chinese cherished allegiance; guarding Xu capital his designs merit record.

value.zh: 不幸早薨，朕甚悼之。
value.en: Unluckily he died young; We greatly mourn him.
value.literal: Unluckily he died young; We greatly mourn him.

value.zh: 今安厝在近，其追贈前將軍。」
value.en: Now that burial is near, let him be posthumously invested as Former General."
value.literal: Now that burial is near, let him be posthumously invested as Former General."

value.zh: 子顒立，徙封河間王，別有傳。
value.en: Heir Yong shifted the fief to Hejian—a fuller life appears in a separate biography.
value.literal: Son Yong succeeded, transferred enfeoffment to Prince of Hejian; elsewhere there is a biography.

value.zh: 高陽元王珪，字子璋，少有才望，魏高陽鄉侯。
value.en: Sima Gui, Prince Yuan of Gaoyang, styled Zizhang, had talent and a good reputation in his youth. Under Wei he was Marquis of Gaoyang Village.
value.literal: Prince Yuan of Gaoyang, Gui, courtesy name Zizhang, had talent and a good reputation in his youth and was Marquis of Gaoyang Township under Wei.

value.zh: 曆河南令，進封湞陽子，拜給事黃門侍郎。
value.en: He governed Henan, rose to Zhenyang viscount, then serving yellow-gate gentleman.
value.literal: He successively held magistrate of Henan, advanced to Viscount of Zhenyang, and was appointed Serving Yellow Gate Gentleman.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封高陽王，邑五千五百七十戶。
value.en: Sima Yan invested Gaoyang at 5,570 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Gaoyang with five thousand five hundred seventy households.

value.zh: 曆北中郎將、督鄴城守諸軍事。
value.en: He commanded northern gentlemen and Ye defenses.
value.literal: He successively held General of the Northern Gentlemen and supervised Ye city garrison affairs.

value.zh: 泰始六年入朝，以父孚年高，乞留供養。
value.en: In the sixth year of Taishi, Court duty moved him to ask leave to nurse elderly Sima Fu.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, Entering court because father Fu was advanced in years he begged to remain and provide support.

value.zh: 拜尚書，遷右僕射。
value.en: He took the ministry then right vice director.
value.literal: He was appointed Minister of Writing and promoted Right Vice Director.

value.zh: 十年薨，詔遣兼大鴻臚持節監護喪事，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司。
value.en: Year ten brought supervised obsequies and posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors matching three-dukes rites.
value.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict dispatched concurrent Grand Herald with credentials to supervise funeral affairs and posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 珪有美譽於世，而帝甚悼惜之。
value.en: Celebrated publicly, he won uncommon imperial grief.
value.literal: Gui had fine reputation in the world yet the emperor deeply mourned and cherished him.

value.zh: 無子，詔以太原王輔子緝襲爵。
value.en: Without issue Taiyuan prince Fu's son Ji inherited.
value.literal: Having no son an edict ordered Prince Fu of Taiyuan's son Ji to inherit the noble rank.

value.zh: 緝立五年，咸寧四年薨，諡曰哀。
value.en: Ji had held the title for five years when he died in Xianning year four, receiving the posthumous epithet Ai.
value.literal: Ji had held the title for five years when he died in Xianning year four, receiving the posthumous epithet Ai.

value.zh: 無子，太康二年詔以太原王瑰世子顒子訟為緝後，封真定縣侯。
value.en: Having no son, in Taikang year two an edict made Song, son of Yong, heir of the heir apparent of Prince Gui of Taiyuan, continue Ji's line and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhending County.
value.literal: Having no son, in Taikang year two an edict made Song, son of Yong, heir of the heir apparent of Prince Gui of Taiyuan, continue Ji's line and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhending County.

value.zh: 常山孝王衡，字子平，魏封德陽鄉侯。
value.en: Sima Heng, styled Ziping, held Deyang village under Wei.
value.literal: Prince Xiao of Changshan Heng courtesy Ziping was Deyang village marquis in Wei.

value.zh: 進封汝陽子，為駙馬都尉。
value.en: Promotion brought Runyang viscount and commandant for princess consorts.
value.literal: He advanced to Viscount of Runyang and became Commandant Steadfast for imperial sons-in-law.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封常山王，邑三千七百九十戶。
value.en: Sima Yan named him Changshan prince at 3,790 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan with three thousand seven hundred ninety households.

value.zh: 二年薨，無子，以安平世子邕第四子敦為嗣。
value.en: Childless after two years Yong's fourth son Dun succeeded.
value.literal: In the second year he died without sons; Yong heir Yong's fourth son Dun was appointed successor.

value.zh: 沛順王景，字子文，魏樂安亭侯。
value.en: Sima Jing, styled Ziwen, began as Leyang ting marquis.
value.literal: Prince Shun of Pei Jing courtesy Ziwen was Leyang precinct marquis in Wei.

value.zh: 曆諫議大夫。
value.en: He served as grand counselor of remonstrance.
value.literal: He successively held Grand Counselor.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封沛王，邑三千四百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan invested Pei at 3,400 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei with three thousand four hundred households.

value.zh: 立十一年，咸寧元年薨，子韜立。
value.en: After holding the title for eleven years, he died in Xianning year one, and his son Tao succeeded.
value.literal: After holding the title for eleven years, he died in Xianning year one, and his son Tao succeeded.

value.zh: 彭城穆王權，字子輿，宣帝弟魏魯相東武城侯馗之子也。
value.en: Sima Quan, King Mu of Pengcheng and styled Ziyu, was the son of Sima Kui, Marquis of Dongwucheng and governor of Lu under Wei, who was Sima Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan courtesy Ziyu was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Lu governor East Wucheng Marquis Kui.

value.zh: 初襲封，拜冗從僕射。
value.en: He opened as supernumerary chariot master.
value.literal: At first inheriting the enfeoffment he was appointed Supernumerary Master of Chariots.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封彭城王，邑二千九百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan made him Pengcheng prince at 2,900 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng with two thousand nine hundred households.

value.zh: 出為北中郎將、都督鄴城守諸軍事。
value.en: He commanded Ye's northern gentleman garrison.
value.literal: He went out as General of the Northern Gentlemen supervising Ye city garrison affairs.

value.zh: 泰始中入朝，賜袞冕之服。
value.en: Mid-Taishi brought court investiture robes.
value.literal: In Taishi mid-years he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state.

value.zh: 咸甯元年薨，子元王植立。
value.en: 275 death; Yuan prince Zhi followed.
value.literal: In Xianning year one he died; son Prince Yuan Zhi succeeded.

value.zh: 歷位後將軍，尋拜國子祭酒、太僕卿、侍中、尚書。
value.en: His offices ran rear general, academy libationer, coach minister, palace attendant, and ministry.
value.literal: He successively held Later General, soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Minister of Coachmanship, palace attendant, and minister of writing.

value.zh: 出為安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，代淮南王允鎮壽春，未發。
value.en: Named east-pacifier for Yangzhou replacing Yun at Shouchun, he never took up post.
value.literal: He was going out as General Who Pacifies the East supervising Yangzhou military affairs replacing Prince Huainan Yun at Shouchun but did not depart.

value.zh: 或云植助允攻趙王倫，遂以憂薨。
value.en: Tradition claims he aided Yun against Sima Lun and died of anxiety.
value.literal: Some say Zhi assisted Yun in attacking Prince Zhao Lun and therefore died of grief.

value.zh: 贈車騎將軍，增封萬五千戶。
value.en: The court added posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors and boosted his fief by fifteen thousand households.
value.literal: He was posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general and his enfeoffment was increased by fifteen thousand households.

value.zh: 子康王釋立，官至南中郎將、持節、平南將軍，分魯國蕃、薛二縣以益其國，心二萬三千戶。
value.en: Prince Kang Sima Shi rose to southern gentleman-general with pacifying-south command, annexed Fan and Xue from Lu, and held twenty-three thousand households.
value.literal: Son Prince Kang Shi succeeded; he reached Southern Gentlemen General, credential-bearing, Pacifying South General; partitioned Fan and Xue counties of Lu to enlarge his state; total twenty-three thousand households.

value.zh: 薨，子雄立，坐奔蘇峻伏誅，更以釋子紘嗣。
value.en: After his death Xiong inherited but died with Su Jun's rebellion; Hong, son of Shi, continued the line.
value.literal: He died; son Xiong succeeded; Xiong was executed for fleeing to Su Jun; Shi's son Hong was changed to succeed.

value.zh: 高密文獻王泰，字子舒，彭城穆王權之弟，魏陽亭侯，補陽翟令，遷扶風太守。
value.en: Sima Tai, styled Zishu, was Sima Quan's brother—Yang ting marquis, Yangdi magistrate, Fufeng governor.
value.literal: Prince Wenxian of Gaomi Tai courtesy Zishu was younger brother of Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan, Marquis of Yang precinct in Wei; supplied Yangdi magistrate; promoted governor of Fufeng.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封隴西王，邑三千二百戶，拜遊擊將軍。
value.en: Sima Yan made him Longxi prince at 3,200 households with roving-strike command.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi with three thousand two hundred households and appointed roving-strike general.

value.zh: 出為兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍。
value.en: He shepherded Yan with hawk-banner general rank.
value.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province with additional general Who Displays Hawk banner.

value.zh: 遷使持節、都督甯益二州諸軍事、安西將軍，領益州刺史，稱疾不行。
value.en: Ning-Yi pacifying-west orders went unfulfilled on grounds of illness.
value.literal: He was promoted credential-bearing supervisor of Ning and Yi military affairs and Pacifying West General concurrent Yi Inspector but pleaded illness and did not go.

value.zh: 轉安北將軍，代兄權督鄴城守事。
value.en: He succeeded brother Quan as pacifying-north chief at Ye.
value.literal: He transferred to Pacifying North General replacing elder brother Quan supervising Ye garrison.

value.zh: 安西將軍、都督關中事。
value.en: He also held pacifying-west charge over Guanzhong.
value.literal: Pacifying West General supervising Guanzhong affairs.

value.zh: 太康初，入為散騎常侍、前將軍，領鄴城門校尉，以疾去官。
value.en: Early Taikang brought palace posts and Ye gate command until illness retired him.
value.literal: Early Taikang he entered as irregular cavalry attendant and former general concurrent colonel of Ye gates but resigned for illness.

value.zh: 後代下邳王晃為尚書左僕射。
value.en: He later succeeded Sima Huang as left vice director.
value.literal: Later he replaced Prince of Xiapi Huang as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 出為鎮西將軍，領護西戎校尉、假節，代扶風王駿都督關中軍事，以疾還京師。
value.en: He was sent out as General Who Guards the West, concurrently Colonel Protector of the Western Rong and Bearer of the Staff, replacing Prince Jun of Fufeng as commander of Guanzhong military affairs, but returned to the capital because of illness.
value.literal: He went out as Guarding West General concurrent colonel of western tribes with credentials replacing Prince of Fufeng Jun supervising Guanzhong military affairs but returned to capital for illness.

value.zh: 永熙初，代石鑒為司空，尋領太子太保。
value.en: Yongxi opened with minister of works and heir-apparent junior tutor posts.
value.literal: Early Yongxi he replaced Shi Jian as Minister of Works and soon concurrent junior tutor to heir apparent.

value.zh: 及楊駿誅，泰領駿營，加侍中，給步兵二千五百人，騎五百匹。
value.en: Jun's purge handed Tai the camp plus two thousand five hundred foot and five hundred horse.
value.literal: When Yang Jun was executed Tai took over Jun's camp with additional palace attendant, two thousand five hundred infantry, and five hundred cavalry granted.

value.zh: 泰固辭，乃給千兵百騎。
value.en: He bargained the guard down to one thousand foot and one hundred horse.
value.literal: Tai firmly declined so only one thousand troops and one hundred cavalry were given.

value.zh: 濟南惠王遂，字子伯，宣帝弟魏鴻臚丞恂之子也。
value.en: Sima Sui, styled Zibo, was Sima Xun's son—Sima Yi's nephew.
value.literal: Prince Hui of Jinan Sui courtesy Zibo was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Grand Herald Assistant Xun.

value.zh: 仕魏關內侯，進封平昌亭侯，曆典軍郎將，
value.en: Under Wei he rose from secondary marquis to Pingchang ting through army posts.
value.literal: Serving Wei district marquis within passes advanced Marquis of Pingchang precinct successively holding army corps captain.

value.zh: 景元二年，轉封武城鄉侯、督鄴城守諸軍事、北中郎將。
value.en: In the second year of Jingyuan, Shifted to Wucheng township marquis guarding Ye as northern gentleman.
value.literal: In the second year of Jingyuan, Transferred enfeoffment Wucheng village marquis supervising Ye garrison Northern Gentlemen General.

value.zh: 五等建，封祝阿伯，累遷冠軍將軍。
value.en: Five-rank reform made him Zhu'e baron then champion general.
value.literal: When five ranks were established enfeoffed Baron of Zhu'e progressively Champion General.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封濟南王。
value.en: Sima Yan created Jinan prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Jinan.

value.zh: 泰始二年薨。
value.en: He died in the second year of Taishi.
value.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he died.

value.zh: 二子：耽、緝。
value.en: Sons Dan and Ji.
value.literal: Two sons: Dan and Ji.

value.zh: 耽嗣立，咸寧三年徙為中山王。
value.en: Dan succeeded to the title, and in Xianning year three he was transferred to be Prince of Zhongshan.
value.literal: Dan succeeded to the title, and in Xianning year three he was transferred to be Prince of Zhongshan.

value.zh: 是年薨，無子，緝繼。
value.en: Dan died childless same year; Ji followed.
value.literal: Same year died without sons Ji continued.

value.zh: 成都王穎以緝為建威將軍，與石熙等率眾距王浚，沒於陣，薨。
value.en: Ying named Ji bulwark general alongside Shi Xi to stop Wang Jun; Ji died on the field.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying appointed Ji bulwark general leading hosts with Shi Xi resisting Wang Jun perishing in battle.

value.zh: 無子，國除。
value.en: Without heirs the principality ended.
value.literal: Having no sons state abolished.

value.zh: 譙剛王遜，字子悌，宣帝弟魏中郎進之子也。
value.en: Sima Xun, styled Ziti, was the son of Sima Jin, Sima Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Prince Gang of Qiao Xun courtesy Ziti was son of Sima Jin—Emperor Xuan's younger brother who served Wei as gentleman of the palace.

value.zh: 仕魏關內侯，改封城陽亭侯，參鎮東軍事，拜輕車將軍、羽林左監。
value.en: Under Wei he rose through marquis ranks to light-chariot general and guard superintendent on the eastern army staff.
value.literal: Serving Wei he held district marquis within the passes, was reassigned marquis of Chengyang precinct, joined the eastern garrison staff, and was appointed general of light chariots and left superintendent of the imperial guard.

value.zh: 五等建，徙封涇陽男。
value.en: Five ranks moved him to Jingyang baron.
value.literal: When five ranks established transferred enfeoffment Jingyang baron.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封譙王，邑四千四百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan made him prince of Qiao at 4,400 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication enfeoffed Prince of Qiao four thousand four hundred households.

value.zh: 泰始二年薨。
value.en: He died in the second year of Taishi.
value.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he died.

value.zh: 二子：隨、承。
value.en: Sons Sui and Cheng.
value.literal: Two sons: Sui and Cheng.

value.zh: 定王隨立。
value.en: Prince Ding Sima Sui inherited.
value.literal: Prince Ding Sui succeeded.

value.zh: 薨，子邃立，沒于石勒，元帝以承嗣遜。
value.en: When the heir was lost to Shi Le, Sima Rui transferred the succession to Sima Cheng.
value.literal: He died; his heir succeeded but fell captive to Shi Le, so Yuan Di appointed Cheng to continue Xun's line.

value.zh: 高陽王睦，字子友，譙王遜之弟也。
value.en: Sima Mu, styled Ziyou, was Sima Xun's brother.
value.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Mu courtesy Ziyou younger brother Prince Qiao Xun.

value.zh: 魏安平亭侯，曆侍御史。
value.en: Under Wei he held Anping ting and censor posts.
value.literal: Wei Anping precinct marquis successively palace attendant investigator.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封中山王，邑五千二百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan made him Zhongshan prince at 5,200 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted abdication enfeoffed Prince of Zhongshan five thousand two hundred households.

value.zh: 睦自表乞依六蓼祀皋陶，鄫杞祀相立廟。
value.en: He sought temples to Gaoyao and Xiang like ancient Liu and Zeng precedents.
value.literal: Mu self memorializing begging rely on Liu liao sacrificing Gaoyao Zeng Qi sacrificing Xiang erecting temples.

value.en: The ministry of rites debated precedent.

value.literal: Doctor libationer Liu Xi etc argued 'Book of Rites Royal Regulations regional marquises five temples two zhao two mu together Grand Progenitor five.

value.en: Suppose branch younger brothers together regional marquises first-enfeoffed lord cannot erect temple.

value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
value.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
value.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

value.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
value.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
value.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

value.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
value.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
value.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

value.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
value.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
value.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

value.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
value.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
value.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

value.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
value.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
value.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

value.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
value.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
value.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

value.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
value.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
value.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

value.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
value.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
value.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, how grievous!
value.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

value.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
value.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
value.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

value.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
value.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
value.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

value.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
value.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
value.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

value.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
value.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
value.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

value.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
value.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
value.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

value.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
value.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
value.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

value.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
value.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
value.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

value.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
value.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
value.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

value.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
value.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
value.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

value.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
value.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
value.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

value.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
value.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
value.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

value.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
value.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
value.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

value.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
value.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
value.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

value.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
value.en: Courtiers weep together.
value.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

value.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
value.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
value.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

value.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
value.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

value.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
value.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
value.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
value.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
value.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

value.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
value.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
value.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

value.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
value.en: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.
value.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.

value.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
value.en: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.
value.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

value.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
value.en: The realm expected greatness.
value.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

value.zh: 及於繼明宸極，守器春坊，四教不勤，三朝或闕，豹姿未變，鳳德已衰，信惑奸邪，疏斥正士，好屠酤之賤役，耽苑囿之佚遊，可謂靡不有初，鮮克有終者也。
value.en: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
value.literal: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

value.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；
value.en: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
value.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

value.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；
value.en: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
value.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

value.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
value.en: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.
value.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.

value.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
value.en: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
value.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

value.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
value.en: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
value.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

value.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
value.en: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
value.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.

value.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
value.en: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.
value.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.

value.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
value.en: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.
value.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.

value.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。
value.en: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
value.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

value.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
value.en: Death ended every hope of restoration.
value.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.

value.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
value.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
value.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

value.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
value.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
value.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.

value.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
value.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
value.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

value.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
value.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
value.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

value.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
value.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
value.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

value.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
value.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
value.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

value.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
value.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
value.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

value.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
value.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
value.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

value.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
value.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
value.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

value.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
value.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
value.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

value.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
value.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
value.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

value.zh: 武帝踐阼，泰始中，粲同郡孫和時為太子中庶子，表薦粲，稱其操行高潔，久嬰疾病，可使郡縣輿致京師，加以聖恩，賜其醫藥，若遂瘳除，必有益於政。
value.en: After Jin Wudi took the throne, Sun He—then junior tutor to the heir apparent and a townsman of Can—memorialized that Can's life was ascetic and his body long ill, that the counties should bring him to Luoyang in a litter, and that imperial physicians might restore him to the state's service.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, in the Taishi years Sun He of Can's commandery, then junior tutor to the heir apparent, submitted a memorial recommending Can, praising his conduct as lofty and pure, long afflicted by illness, and saying the commandery and county could carry him in a litter to the capital; if the sagely favor granted him medicine and he then recovered, he would surely benefit governance.

value.zh: 乃詔郡縣給醫藥，又以二千石祿養病，歲以為常，加賜帛百匹。
value.en: The throne ordered local officials to furnish physic and pay him a two-thousand-bushel stipend year after year to nurse his health, plus a hundred rolls of silk.
value.literal: An edict then ordered the commandery and county to supply medicine, and also to support his illness with the salary of a two-thousand-bushel rank, yearly as a rule, adding a gift of one hundred bolts of silk.

value.zh: 子喬以父疾篤，辭不敢受，詔不許。
value.en: His son Fan Qiao, thinking the sickness grave, tried to decline the bounty; the edict refused the refusal.
value.literal: His son Qiao, because his father's illness was grave, declined and dared not accept; the edict did not permit refusal.

value.zh: 乙太康六年卒，時年八十四，不言三十六載，終於所寢之車。
value.en: He died in Taikang 6 at eighty-four, having kept silence thirty-six years, and breathed his last in the cart that was his bed.
value.literal: He died in the sixth year of Taikang at age eighty-four; for thirty-six years he did not speak, and ended in the carriage in which he slept.

value.zh: 長子喬。
value.en: His eldest son was Fan Qiao.
value.literal: The eldest son was Qiao.

value.zh: 郭琦，字公偉，太原晉陽人也。
value.en: Guo Qi, courtesy name Gongwei, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.
value.literal: Guo Qi, styled Gongwei, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

value.zh: 少方直，有雅量，博學，善五行，作《天文志》、《五行傳》，注《穀梁》、《京氏易》百卷。
value.en: Young, upright, and learned in astrology, he wrote treatises on heaven, the five phases, and a hundred fascicles on the Guliang and Jing Changes.
value.literal: In youth he was square and straight, had a refined capacity, was broadly learned, skilled in the five phases, and composed the Monograph on Heaven, the Traditions of the Five Phases, and a hundred rolls of commentary on the Guliang Annals and the Jing family Changes.

value.zh: 鄉人王遊等皆就琦學。
value.en: Townsmen such as Wang You studied at his feet.
value.literal: His townsman Wang You and others all came to Qi to study.

value.zh: 武帝欲以琦為佐著作郎，問琦族人尚書郭彰。
value.en: Emperor Wu meant to name him assistant editor and asked his kinsman Guo Zhang.
value.literal: Emperor Wu wished to make Qi assistant editorialist and asked Qi's clansman Minister Guo Zhang.

value.zh: 彰素疾琦，答云：「不識」。
value.en: Zhang hated him and said flatly, 'I never heard of him.'
value.literal: Zhang by nature detested Qi and answered, "I do not know him."

value.zh: 帝曰：「若如卿言，烏丸家兒能事卿，即堪為郎矣。」
value.en: The emperor retorted, 'If a Wuhuan stable-boy is good enough for you, he is good enough for my editorial office.'
value.literal: The emperor said, "If it is as you say, then a Wuhuan household lad who can serve you would be fit to be a gentleman!"

value.zh: 遂決意用之。
value.en: So the emperor appointed Qi anyway.
value.literal: Thereupon he resolved to employ him.

value.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，又欲用琦，琦曰：「我已為武帝吏，不容復為今世吏。」
value.en: When Sima Lun seized the throne and offered a post, Qi answered, "I served Emperor Wu; I will not serve your court."
value.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun usurped the throne, he again wished to use Qi; Qi said, "I have already been an official to Emperor Wu; I cannot again be an official to today's world."

value.zh: 終身處於家。
value.en: He stayed home for life.
value.literal: To the end of his life he remained at home.

value.zh: 慕容暐
value.en: Murong Wei
value.literal: Murong Wei (section heading).

value.zh: 始廆以武帝太康六年稱公，至暐四世。
value.en: Murong Gui first received the ducal title in the sixth year of Taikang under Jin Wudi; to Murong Wei was four generations.
value.literal: At first Gui in Emperor Wu's sixth year of Taikang was called duke; reaching Wei was four generations.

value.zh: 暐在位一十一年，以海西公太和五年滅，通廆、皝凡八十五年。
value.en: Murong Wei reigned eleven years; the state fell in the fifth year of Taihe under the Duke of Haixi—eighty-five years in all from Murong Gui and Murong Huang.
value.literal: Wei on the throne eleven years; with Duke of Haixi in the fifth year of Taihe destroyed—through Gui and Huang altogether eighty-five years.

value.zh: 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 上官儀
value.en: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Shang Guanyi
value.literal: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Shang Guanyi

value.zh: 古之聖王，立諫鼓，設謗木，冀欲聞逆耳之言，甘苦口之議，發揚大化，裨益洪猷，垂令譽於將來，播休聲於不朽者也。
value.en: The sage kings of antiquity established remonstrance drums and set up slander posts, hoping to hear ear-offending words and welcome bitter counsel, to extend great transformation and benefit vast plans, to hang fine reputation on the future and spread excellent fame for eternity.
value.literal: The sage kings of antiquity established remonstrance drums and set up slander posts, hoping to hear ear-offending words and sweet bitter-mouth discussions, to extend great transformation and benefit vast plans, to hang fine reputation on the future and spread excellent sound in imperishability.

value.zh: 伏見詔書以褚遂良為潭州都督，臣夙夜思之，用增感激。
value.en: I see the edict making Chu Suiliang Area Commander of Tanzhou. Day and night I have pondered it, and my emotion and gratitude have only increased.
value.literal: I prostrate and see the edict making Chu Suiliang Area Commander of Tanzhou—this subject day and night pondered it, thereby increasing emotion and gratitude.

value.zh: 臣識慚知遠，業謝通經，載撫愚情，誠為未可。
value.en: My knowledge is ashamed before knowing the far, and my craft declines before mastering the classics. Bearing my foolish feelings, I truly cannot remain silent.
value.literal: This subject's knowledge is ashamed before knowing the far, my craft declines before mastering the classics—bearing and stroking foolish feeling, truly it cannot be done.

value.zh: 遂良運偶昇平，道昭前烈，束髮從宦，方淹累稔。
value.en: Suiliang's fate met an age of ascending peace, and his Way illuminated former worthies. From binding his hair he followed office, submerged in service for many accumulated years.
value.literal: Suiliang's fate met ascending peace, his Way illuminated former worthies; binding hair he followed office, just submerged for accumulated years.

value.zh: 趨侍陛下，俄歷歲年，不聞涓滴之愆，常睹勤勞之效。
value.en: Hastening to attend Your Majesty, he has shortly passed many years. Not a drop's fault has been heard of him, and the effects of his diligent toil are constantly seen.
value.literal: Hastening to attend Your Majesty, shortly passing years and years—not heard a drop's fault, constantly seen diligent toil's effect.

value.zh: 竭忠誠於早歲，罄直道於茲年。
value.en: He exhausted his loyalty in early years and spent the straight Way in this year.
value.literal: He exhausted loyalty in early years, spent the straight Way in this year.

value.zh: 體國忘家，捐身徇物，風霜其操，鐵石其心。
value.en: He embodied the state and forgot his family, casting away his body to follow public affairs. Wind and frost were his conduct, and iron and stone his heart.
value.literal: Embodying the state and forgetting family, casting away the body to follow affairs—wind and frost his conduct, iron and stone his heart.

value.zh: 誠可重於皇明，詎專方於曩昔？
value.en: Truly he can be valued in your imperial brilliance—how could he be valued only in former times?
value.literal: Truly he can be valued in imperial brilliance—how only specialized in former times?

value.zh: 且先帝納之於帷幄，寄之以心膂，德逾水石，義冠舟車，公家之利，言無不可。
value.en: Moreover the former emperor admitted him into the tent curtains and entrusted him with heart and backbone. His virtue exceeded water and stone, and his righteousness crowned boats and chariots. For the public family's benefit, in speech nothing was not permissible.
value.literal: Moreover the former emperor admitted him into the tent curtains, entrusted him with heart and backbone—virtue exceeding water and stone, righteousness crowning boats and chariots; the public family's benefit, in speech nothing not permissible.

value.zh: 及纏悲四海，遏密八音，竭忠國家，親承顧托，一德無二，千古懍然。
value.en: When grief enveloped the four seas and the eight tones were stilled, he exhausted his loyalty for the state and personally received the dying entrustment. One virtue without duality—for a thousand ages awe-inspiring.
value.literal: When grief enveloped the four seas and eight tones were stilled, he exhausted loyalty for the state, personally received the dying entrustment—one virtue without duality, for a thousand ages awe-inspiring.

value.zh: 此不待臣言，陛下備知之矣。
value.en: This does not await my words—Your Majesty is fully aware of it.
value.literal: This does not await this subject's words—Your Majesty is fully aware.

value.zh: 臣嘗有此心，未敢聞奏。
value.en: I once had this thought in my heart but dared not memorialize it.
value.literal: This subject once had this heart but dared not hear and memorialize.

value.zh: 且萬姓失業，旰食忘勞；
value.en: Moreover the myriad people have lost their occupations, and you eat late and forget fatigue;
value.literal: Moreover the myriad names lose their occupations, eating late and forgetting fatigue;

value.zh: 一物不安，納隍軫慮，在於微細，寧得過差。
value.en: if one thing is not at peace, you receive it into the moat and turn your care. In what is minute and fine, how can there be excess error?
value.literal: one thing not at peace, receiving the moat and turning care—in what is minute and fine, how can there be excess error.

value.zh: 況社稷之舊臣，陛下之賢佐，無聞罪狀，斥去朝廷，內外氓黎，咸嗟舉措。
value.en: How much more a former minister of the altars of state and Your Majesty's worthy assistant—no crime heard of, yet expelled from court. Inner and outer common folk all sigh at this action.
value.literal: How much more a former minister of the altars of state, Your Majesty's worthy assistant—no crime heard, expelled from court; inner and outer common folk all sigh at the action.

value.zh: 觀其近日言事，披誠懇切，詎肯後陛下之德，異於堯、舜；
value.en: Observing his recent words on affairs, spreading sincerity earnest and cutting—how would he lag behind Your Majesty's virtue or differ from Yao and Shun;
value.literal: Observing his recent days' speaking on affairs, spreading sincerity earnest and cutting—how would he lag behind Your Majesty's virtue, differ from Yao and Shun;

value.zh: 懼陛下之過，塵於史冊。
value.en: he fears only that Your Majesty's excess will stain the historical records.
value.literal: he fears Your Majesty's excess will dust the historical records.

value.zh: 而乃深遭厚謗，重負丑言，可以痛志士之心，損陛下之明也。
value.en: Yet he deeply suffers thick slander and heavily bears ugly words. This can pain the heart of a determined scholar and diminish Your Majesty's brilliance.
value.literal: Yet he deeply suffers thick slander, heavily bears ugly words—this can pain the determined scholar's heart and diminish Your Majesty's brilliance.

value.zh: 臣聞晉武弘裕，不貽劉毅之誅；
value.en: I have heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was vast and generous and did not bequeath punishment to Liu Yi;
value.literal: This subject has heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was vast and generous, not bequeathing Liu Yi's punishment;

value.zh: 漢祖深仁，無恚周昌之直。
value.en: the Han Founder was deeply benevolent and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's straightness.
value.literal: the Han Founder was deeply benevolent, without resentment toward Zhou Chang's straightness.

value.zh: 而遂良被遷，已經寒暑，違忤陛下，其罰塞焉。
value.en: Yet Suiliang has been transferred and has already passed through cold and heat. Having offended Your Majesty, his punishment is sufficient.
value.literal: Yet Suiliang was transferred, already passing cold and heat; having offended Your Majesty, his punishment is sufficient.

value.zh: 伏願纟面鑑無辜，稍寬非罪，俯矜微款，以順人情。
value.en: I beg you to look down with compassion on the innocent, slightly loosen what is not truly a crime, bow to cherish his slight sincerity, and accord with human feeling.
value.literal: I prostrate myself wishing to look down and examine the innocent, slightly loosen non-crime, bowing to cherish slight sincerity, to accord with human feelings.
